content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day horizon.
- Model tends to overreact to recent spikes (e.g., 70+ values) by overshooting into higher forecasts, then corrects too late.
- Forecasts often lag behind true values by 1–3 days, particularly in the first 5–7 days of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: after a sharp spike, it overcorrects downward, missing the true continuation of the trend.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the final 5–7 days, underestimating the true price decline or stabilization.
- Model fails to capture the “tail” of the price distribution — especially when true values show a sharp drop or plateau after a peak.
- Forecasts are sensitive to recent low values — model tends to “hold” low prices longer than they should, even when history shows upward momentum.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of true price increases after a dip, especially in the 10–15 day window.
